title: Canary Lifeline Controller with Probationary Rollforward Scorer
author: Marina Kovács
body: Context and motivation: We observed frequent noisy canaries where short-lived anomalies caused either unnecessary rollbacks or prolonged manual interventions. This PR implements the "Canary Lifeline" controller: a probationary rollforward flow that allows a canary to progress under strict probation rules and applies a probabilistic rollback scorer when signals deteriorate. It reduces manual triage and allows safe, granular promotion of models in high-traffic environments. Design summary: The controller introduces two runtime primitives: (1) probationary windows that allow ephemeral metric volatility without immediate rollback, and (2) a probabilistic rollforward scorer that computes a confidence score for promoting or auto-reverting a canary based on multi-signal aggregation (latency P95, error-rate, model-quality delta, cost-per-token). Scoring is temporally weighted so recently improving signals are favored while persistent regressions escalate the rollback probability. Implementation highlights: - New controller: redwood/orchestrator/canary_lifeline.go implements the probation lifecycle (phases: seed, probation, verification, commit, rewind) and hooks into the existing rollout engine. - Probationary scoring engine: redwood/orchestrator/rollforward_scorer.go provides modular signal adapters and a configurable scoring policy (decay half-life, threshold bands, escalation multiplier). - API types: redwood/api/v1/rollout_types.go extends RolloutSpec with probationConfig and rollforwardPolicy fields. - Console: a small UI panel redwood/console/ui/rollouts/CanaryLifelinePanel.tsx surfaces score trajectories and suggests human action buttons (hold, promote, abort). - Tests and docs: integration tests under redwood/tests/integration/canary_lifeline_test.go plus a runbook at redwood/docs/runbooks/canary-lifeline.md. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior preserves existing rollout semantics when probationConfig is omitted. The controller is gated behind a feature flag rollout.control.canary_lifeline=false by default in config. Migration plan: - Canary Lifeline is off by default. - Early adopters can opt in per-namespace and pin policy parameters. - We'll run a staged internal rollout (dev -> staging -> controlled pilot) and monitor the new metrics introduced (probation_score, probation_duration_ms, rollforward_invocations). Testing and validation: Unit tests for scoring logic, simulated traffic harness for stochastic evaluation, and two integration smoke runs against the test cluster were added. CI: initial lint failure on TypeScript formatting fixed in follow-up commit; full pipeline green after rerun. Rollout/runbook: The docs include an operator playbook with recommended thresholds, synthetic smoke commands, and a retro-triage checklist for policy tuning. Observability: New metrics and tracing spans were added; the Console panel links to raw traces and the Eval set diff used for model-quality calculations. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: overly permissive probation could hide regressions. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and a visible probation_score below 0.35 triggers auto-quarantine. - Risk: score drift due to noisy metrics. Mitigation: configurable decay and an anomaly-detection prefilter that gates signals. Related work and references: ENG-2439: probationary-rollforward-scorer (design); ENG-2501: rollout-metrics-unification. Files changed (high-level): see files_changed list for exact paths. Merge notes: squashed into main. Post-merge actions: schedule a six-week pilot with SLA-backed teams and create an alert for probation_score anomalies to the SRE rotations.
